newsitem.title: POLAND: Dlr gains, foreign sales squash zloty, depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Dlr gains, foreign sales squash zloty, depos ease.

text.p: The zloty softened against the currency basket on Thursday as an early bout of foreign investor sales of Polish T-bills and the U.S. dollar's gains depressed the local currency, dealers said.
They said the zloty was also pushed down by banks which extended hard currency positions cut on Wednesday following a severe but short-lived zloty shortage on the money market.
"Players started the day on the short-side and followed the dollar's ride up against the mark following the Bank of France's statement," said Maciej Grabosz of Bank Zachodni SA.
Earlier today a member of the French central bank's board said the dollar should be stronger against the German mark and send the U.S. unit soaring in European trade to 1.5340 marks.
The zloty closed at 2.09/2.03 percent from the trading band centre down from Wednesday's close at 2.29/2.24 percent.
It was at 2.8470/85 to the dollar, down from 2.8320/30 on Wednesday and at 1.8570/81 to the mark, up from 1.8580/90.
Dealers expected the zloty to drift mostly sideways on Friday as the zloty returned to the middle of its weeks-long trading band between 1.8 and 2.3 percent from the parity rate.
Trade was light on the secondary T-bill market with the only movement coming from foreign investors, who sold small amounts of paper with some three-months to maturity.

Overnight rates eased to 18.80/19.15 percent from opening's 19.25/19.55 percent as the money market showed no signs of liquidity problems going into Friday -- the last day of November's required reserve period.
Tomorrow/next rates closed at 19.00/19.40 percent, barely changed from opening's 19.00/19.45 despite today's 551 million zlotys 14-day reverse repo.
